disqualifiers.reason: No identified pain means no reason to act on any timeline; this is not an opportunity yet

criteria.label: Metrics
criteria.note: Scores what the metric IS, not whether one exists. A metric the seller invented does not survive the buyer's internal review, so it scores barely above nothing.

criteria.label: Economic buyer
criteria.note: Weighted highest. Knowing who the economic buyer is scores 1, not 3 — identification without access is the most over-credited state in pipeline review.

criteria.label: Decision criteria
criteria.note: Criteria you inferred may be criteria a competitor wrote.

criteria.label: Paper process
criteria.note: Six weeks of security review discovered in the last week of the quarter is the most common single-cause slip in enterprise software.

criteria.label: Identified pain
criteria.note: Pain without a deadline loses to every competing priority. Its most common competitor is not a rival vendor, it is 'next year'.

criteria.label: Champion
criteria.note: Tested means they have done something costly for you: taken a meeting to their boss, shared internal information, put their name on something. Someone friendly on calls is a coach.

criteria.label: Competition
criteria.note: Remember that 'do nothing' is usually the leading competitor.
